drafted_from: tool row in tools/start-a-computer/tool-rows.json, do-work/start-a-computer.mjs (rentAMachine) and tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Rent me a builder machine at 192.0.2.41 under the name a-builder, point releases.example.com at it, and tell me when it answers SSH."
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads a request file and its provider rows, and writes one lease file.
instructions: 1. Write request.json: lease_file, machine {provider, name, placement, lifetime}, name {host_name} (and name.provider and zone to make a DNS record), ssh {known_hosts}. A machine you already run uses provider "existing-machine" with placement.address.

2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:rent-a-machine"} and runs node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs rent request.json, with provider credentials on descriptors 3 and 4 when the provider rents.
3. Read the JSON line: lease, host_name, arch and price. Nothing is set up on the machine; hand the lease to the tool that builds on it. Run again to resume from the saved lease.
4. Give it back later with tool:give-back-a-computer and the same lease file.

worked_examples.title: A machine the person already runs is leased and waited for
worked_examples.ask: Take my spare machine as a builder and tell me its architecture.
worked_examples.given: From tools/start-a-computer/test/start-a-computer.test.mjs ('renting a machine leases it and waits for SSH, and sets nothing up on it'). request.json = {"lease_file":"lease.json","machine":{"provider":"existing-machine","name":"a-builder","placement":{"address":"192.0.2.41"},"lifetime":"service"},"name":{"host_name":"releases.example.com"},"ssh":{"known_hosts":"known_hosts"}}. The only command run on the machine is uname -m, which says x86_64. Run: node tools/start-a-computer/do-work/start-a-computer.mjs rent request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"lease":{"provider":"existing-machine","name":"a-builder","address":"192.0.2.41","state":"running"},"host_name":"releases.example.com","arch":"x86_64","price":null}: lease.json now holds address 192.0.2.41, so tool:give-back-a-computer can forget it.
